description:
### User Story

As an Estimator, I need the system to generate standardized, fixed-format reports for Cost and Carbon estimates, ensuring they accurately reflect the estimate data, so that I can provide consistent and compliant reports for review, approval, and record-keeping.

### Context

The solution will be able to produce fixed, non-user-configurable reports for both Cost and Carbon estimates. These reports are essential for formal documentation, review processes, and archival purposes within National Highways.

CESS reports serve as tools for financial management and project control. They provide estimators and project managers with a structured view of project costs, enabling them to track expenses, analyse cost breakdowns, and forecast future expenditures. By presenting cost data in various formats and levels of detail, CESS reports facilitate informed decision-making regarding budgeting, resource allocation, and cost optimization throughout the project lifecycle. 

CCESS reports expand upon the functionality of CESS reports by integrating carbon-related information, making them essential for assessing and managing the environmental impact of projects. In addition to cost analysis, CCESS reports enable users to quantify, track, and analyse carbon emissions, supporting sustainable project delivery and environmental compliance. These reports are crucial for evaluating the carbon footprint of different project activities, and reporting on carbon reduction progress, ultimately driving more environmentally responsible decision-making. 

Historically, Cost and Carbon estimates have been reported on separately, however will now be delivered in a consolidated report that covers both cost and carbon estimates. Given both the CESS report (Cost Estimate Summary Sheet Report) and CCESS (Cost and Carbon Estimate Summary Sheet Report) have been classed as fixed reports, it is required that their structure (and the data they contain) are predefined and not subject to modification by the estimator. This will ensure consistency and compliance with National Highways' standards.


### Acceptance Criteria

1. Reports are identical/ follow the structure of the mock ups provided (see attached mock ups)

2. Reports will be exportable as MS Excel (.xlsx format)

3. Reports will contain a title or description 

4. Users can identify the project name(s), estimates name(s) and estimate ID(s) within the reports . (Refer to report mock up)

5. Basic project details are visible within the report to identify which scheme it is from

6. Reporting data will be formatted in a way that is easy to follow 

7. The reports accurately reflect the data within the corresponding Cost and Carbon estimates. (Chapter 8)   

8. Access to Reports/Exports is available from either a ‘global reporting menu’ or from the ‘screen specific reporting menu’, e.g. if in the ‘review’ screen, users have quick access available to those reports directly relevant to the activity they are performing on that screen, e.g. review estimate.


Note: For Release 1b given the 3-point estimate capability for V10 is not currently available, the min, most likely and Max values will not be included in the report, however  the deterministic value will be mapped to the “most likely” column.

summary: Estimator - Set Estimate Price Base Date (Cost) and Estimate Base Date (Carbon) UI
description:
As an Estimator, I want to set a common price base date and a common carbon base date for my entire estimate in the estimate details, so that all item costs and carbon values can be normalized to a single, consistent point in time.

• Description: This is a critical step for ensuring all costs in an estimate are comparable. After the creation of a new estimate, the estimator must define a single "common price base date" and a "common carbon base date" in the estimate details . This date acts as the target to which all individual item costs will be adjusted (rebased), regardless of their original price base. This provides a consistent financial baseline for the entire project.

• Acceptance Criteria:
• When viewing the estimate details, there is a mandatory field for the estimator to enter a "Common Price Base Date" and a "common carbon base date".

• The "common carbon base date" is defaulted to 2020 but can be overwritten by the estimator

• The estimator can select a date using a calendar picker.

• The estimate cannot be fully created until this date has been provided.

• This date is stored at the estimate level and is used as the target date for all rebasing

summary: Estimator - Estimate summary configuration - Define Project Milestones/ Schedules  etc UI
description:
User Story 

As an Estimator, I need to define the Start (ML) and End (ML) dates for each project stage and ensure the associated Cost Elements automatically inherit and validate these dates, 

I want to define specific Inflation Indices (for Cost and Carbon) and set other parameters for each Cost Element, overriding the defaults, so that my estimate's financial modeling and reporting are highly accurate and specific to the project. so that the estimate accurately aligns all costs with the project timeline.


Acceptance Criteria 

### Access & Navigation

• The "Estimate Summary Configuration" option is visible and accessible in the Tools  via the NH Functions menu option  of the main project view.

### Estimate Stages & Milestones

• The configuration grid must display a list of project stages (e.g. PCF Stage 0, PCF Stage 1) that are relevant to the project's lifecycle, as defined in the standard codes library.

• The header for the project stages must be titled “Milestones”.

• Under each project stage, the associated Cost Elements, adhering to the defined NH structure, must be visible.

• For each stage, the user can input dates into the "Start (ML)" (Most Likely) and "End (ML)" columns.

• Clicking a date input field must display a date picker calendar.

• Stage Date Validation: The system must validate that the End (ML) date is not earlier than the Start (ML) date for the same stage.

• The overall project start and end dates will be automatically derived from the earliest Start (ML) date and latest End (ML) date entered across all stages.

• Start and End dates for different stages can overlap.

### Cost Element Start and End Dates & Configuration

• CE Date Default: The Start/End (ML) dates for a Cost Element must automatically default from the relevant parent project stage.

• CE Date Override: The Cost Element Start/End dates must remain editable at the Cost Element level, allowing the Estimator to override the cascaded stage dates.

### Cost Element Base Date & Configuration

• CE Base Date: The CE Base Date (Cost Element Base Date) must automatically pull its default value from the settings defined by the Admin in the Cost Element Library.

• CE Base Date Override: For each Cost Element, the Estimator can override the default CE Base Date using a date picker calendar.

### Inflation Index Configuration (Cost & Carbon)

• Inflation Index (Cost):
• The default Inflation Index (Cost) must be automatically pulled from the default settings defined by the Admin in the Cost Element Library.

• The Estimator can update this default by selecting from a list of available indices in the existing Inflation Library via a dropdown option.

• Inflation Index (Carbon) CO2e
• The default Inflation Index (Carbon) must be pulled from the default settings defined by the Admin in the Cost Element Library.

• The Estimator can update this default by selecting from a list of available indices in the existing Inflation Library via a dropdown option.

### B. Variance (Var) Parameters

• Min/Max Var % (Cost):
• The Min Var % and Max Var % fields must be editable, allowing the Estimator to enter a maximum variance value.

• The input format must allow for three decimal places (e.g. 9.999).

• Both Min Var % and Max Var % must be defaulted to 0.000 for this Epic.

• Min/Max Var % (Carbon):
• The Min Var %  CO2e and Max Var %CO2e fields must be present and follow the same logic as the Cost variance fields (editable, 9.999 format, default to 0.000).

### C. Spend Profile Visibility & Override

• Profile Selection: The "Spend Profile Type" dropdown allows the Estimator to select a standard spend profile type (or a bespoke profile) for the selected scheme type to apply to a Cost Element.

• Profile Details: The spend profile section can be collapsed and expanded to view the percentage split for the selected profile type and scheme type.

• Editing Restriction: Editing of the percentage split values, the default scheme type, or defining a bespoke spend profile must be completed solely via the "Manage Expenditure Profiles" menu option (as defined in the previous Epic refinement).

• Historic Status: A non-editable field must provide the Estimator visibility of whether the Cost Element is flagged as a Historic Cost Element.

### D. System Scope & Prerequisites

• Any overrides made by the Estimator (dates, indices, profiles) apply only to the current estimate and do not alter the Admin's master defaults.

• The system must store the updated Cost Element configuration against the Estimator's current estimate, and this configuration must drive the estimate's reporting structure.

• Prerequisite: The Estimate Summary Configuration must be completed (validated) prior to the successful calculation of the Inflation Summary and Overall Estimate Summary.

summary: Trigger CCESS Reporting and complete validation - UI
description:
Description: As an Estimator, I need the system to run a series of automated checks before generating the report, so that I can identify and fix data issues and prevent errors in the final output. These checks ensure that the data is sufficient and correctly configured.

Acceptance Criteria:

• The system shall provide a Checklist sub-tab for the CCESS Generator tab.

• A button labeled [Run Exceptions Check] will trigger the validation process.

• The system will perform the following checks, displaying a corresponding label and error message if the check fails:
• Check 1: Hierarchy Check: A cost element cannot be nested under another cost element.
• Check Label: Checking compatibility of Composite Total hierarchy.

• Error Message: "Cost Element [XYZ] is nested under another Cost Element [ABC]. CCESS cannot be generated due to incompatible hierarchy structure of items."

• Check 2: Item Code Alignment: All costs within a section must be accounted for on the CCESS
• Check Label: Checking alignment between Item Codes and Project Cost Element codes.

• Error Message: "Cost of Section [ABC] in the project will not match with the cost of this section on CESS. Please check and confirm alignment of Cost Element Codes with corresponding Item Codes of Composite Totals in the project."

• Check 3: Inflation Data: Valid inflation indices must be assigned to all cost elements with a cost value.
• Check Label: Confirming availability of inflation index values.

• Error Message: "Insufficient inflation data for Cost Element [ABC]. Please ensure inflation data corresponding to Cost Base Date of Cost Element [ABC] and Project Details → Cost Base Date are configured correctly in the system."

• Check 4: The Value  percentages for  NRVAT must be present
• Check Label: Validating Non-Recoverable VAT percentages.

• Error Message: "No NRVAT%  found in Project Details. Please ensure that NRVAT %has been populated"

• Check 5: Historic Cost Check: Historic Cost Elements must be excluded from simulation
• Check Label: Validating settings of Historic Cost Elements.

• Error Message: "Exclude from Simulation checkbox in Project → Items is unchecked against the Composite Total corresponding to Historic Cost Element [ABC]. Please check the Exclude from Simulation checkbox against Composite Total [DEF] in Section [XYZ]."

• Check 6: Section to Cost Element Hierarchy
• Check Label: Validating Section - Cost Element hierarchy in the project.

• Error Message: "Composite Totals corresponding to Cost Element [ABC] is present in more than one Section. CCESS cannot be generated due to incompatible Item hierarchy structure."

• Check 7: Hierarchy Uniqueness: A cost element cannot be in more than one section, and section descriptions must be unique.
• Check Label: Validating duplicate Section descriptions.

• Error Message: "Section Description [ABC] is has been used in more than one Section. CCESS cannot be generated due to incompatible Item hierarchy structure."

• Checkboxes will be automatically ticked for passed checks, and an information icon will display the corresponding error message for failed checks.

Rebase Estimate  Costs and Carbon - UI
description:
User Story:

As an Estimator, I need the system to automatically perform normalization for cost and carbon... when I Inflation, So that the final estimate is presented in a consistent price base year.

Acceptance Criteria:

• Trigger: The Rebasing calculation is triggered automatically after the "Generate Inflation Summary" button is successfully pressed and all validation checks have passed.

• For Cost: For each cost element, the system must calculate:

• Rebased Cost = Original Cost * (Index at Estimate Common Base Date / Index at Cost Element Base Date)
• This calculation is worked out based on Cost Element Total Cost (Base(Including UIA) + Project Risk + Uncertainty + Programme Risk + Portfolio Risk)

• Worked Example:
• Original Cost Element Cost = £100,000

• Cost Element Base Date = Q1 2023 (Index Value: 100)

• Estimate Common Base Date = Q1 2025 (Index Value: 110)

• Rebased Cost=  = £100,000 * (110 / 100) = £110,000

• For Carbon (Modeled): For each item, the system must calculate:
• Rebased Carbon = Item Quantity * Carbon Emission Factor

• For Carbon (Cost to Carbon - CTC): For each item, the system must calculate:
• Rebased Carbon = (Original Cost * (Index at Est. Common Carbon Base Date / Index at CE Base Date)) * CTC Factor

• Output: The resulting Rebased Cost and Rebased Carbon values are stored and used as the input for the final outturn calculations.

• Non-Application: The rebasing calculation is not applied to any costs designated as Historic Costs.

description:
User Story 

As an Estimator, I want the system to automatically calculate the final outturn cost, so that I have a complete and accurate cost estimate...

Acceptance Criteria:

• This calculation is triggered automatically after Rebasing

• For each cost element, the system must retrieve its Rebased Cost,  its assigned Spend Profile  and its final Project Start/End Dates.

• The system must distribute the Rebased Cost across the time periods  according to the Spend Profile percentages.

• For each time period, the system must calculate the inflation:
• Inflation for Period = (Rebased Cost * Spend % for Period) * ((Index at Spend Period / Index at Est. Base Date) - 1)

• The system must sum the inflation from all periods to get Total Future Inflation.

• The system must calculate the final cost displayed in the report:
• Outturn Cost = Rebased Cost + Total Future Inflation

Goal: To fully integrate Programme and Portfolio Risk into the Cost and Carbon Estimating System (CCES) by enabling the application of predefined, mandatory risk percentages to eligible Cost Elements within an estimate (bottom-up calculation), and providing accurate aggregate reporting and compliance outputs (CCESS).

User Value: Ensures all estimates comply with National Highways’ financial reporting standards by including mandated strategic risk allowances, reducing manual effort, and providing clear, auditable cost and carbon totals before inflation.

### Key Capabilities

1. Risk Library Administration :
• Implement an administrative function to allow Estimating Managers to upload and store distinct Programme and Portfolio Risk percentage matrices (Cost and Carbon) for all major estimate types (MP CapEx, AR CapEx, O&M, LTA) and their corresponding lifecycle stages.

• This function must allow mapping of the risk percentages to specific Cost Elements to control where the allowance is applied.

2. Estimate Calculation & Application :
• The system must automatically calculate the Programme and Portfolio Risk allowances for an estimate by applying the correct percentage (based on the estimate's lifecycle stage and chosen risk profile) to the Estimate Total (Base Cost + Project Risk + Uncertainty) of the eligible Cost Elements.

• Carbon risk must be derived from the calculated Cost Risk using the Cost-to-Carbon factor for the same Cost Element (FR1090).

3. Reporting & Display :

• The final Estimate Summary and CCESS output must display the calculated Programme and Portfolio Risk allowances as separate line items before the application of inflation.

• The system must calculate and display a high-level "Rollup Risk Percentage" in summary dashboards. This percentage is a bottom-up metric for display only (calculated as: Total PP Risk Cost Allowance / Total Scheme Cost Excluding PP Risk) and must not be used for top-down calculation.

This Epic defines the framework for vetting cost and carbon estimates before they are formally authorized. The objective is to move away from informal, manual review processes toward a structured, system-driven workflow that ensures every estimate is scrutinized by the correct experts and senior leadership. It covers everything from the initial assignment of reviewers to the final "Approval" action that locks the estimate data.

### Key Functional Pillars

### 1. Collaborative Parallel Reviewing

The workflow supports a multi-reviewer model where Peer, Project Team, and Estimating Manager reviewers can work simultaneously. This removes the "wait-time" associated with traditional linear workflows. Key to this specialism is the ability to assign separate reviewers for Cost and Carbon components, ensuring specialists focus on their respective areas of expertise.

### 2. Dynamic Assignment & Overrides

Flexibility is built into the initiation phase, allowing Estimating Managers to assign a review team from an authorized library. Recognizing that project timelines change, the system allows Estimators to "override" or update these assignments post-initiation to account for staff leave or resource shifts, provided the new reviewer is selected from the authorized library.

### 3. Structured Feedback (The Review Modal)

Reviewers interact with a dedicated Review Modal where they must select a formal status (Approved, Approved with Comments, or Rejected) and provide free-text feedback. This ensures that the Estimator receives clear, actionable guidance. Every interaction is captured with a permanent time/date stamp, creating a transparent audit trail.

### 4. The Approval Gateway & Data Locking

Once the vetting stage is complete, the Estimator moves the status to "Ready for Approval." This notifies a senior Authorized Approver. The final approval action is a critical system gate:

• Data Integrity: Upon final approval, the estimate is locked, preventing any further edits to the figures.

• Traceability: The system records the final authorization signature and timestamp, which is automatically mapped to the CE300 form.

• Downstream Trigger: Only a status of "Approved" enables the subsequent "Issue Estimate" functionality.

### 5. Auditability and Monitoring (Review Log)

All comments, statuses, and timestamps are aggregated into a centralized Review Log. This log provides a single source of truth for the estimate’s history. Additionally, high-level progress is tracked in the Estimate Browser, allowing managers to see at a glance where an estimate is in the review lifecycle (e.g. Ready for Review vs. Reviews in Progress).

We need a centralised, declarative way to manage API authorisation. Instead of checking permissions inside every controller/handler, we want a configuration-based "framework" that intercepts requests and validates permissions based on the HTTP Method and Endpoint.

User Story

• As a Backend Developer,

• I want to define permissions in a single configuration file mapping Routes + Methods to required Roles/Scopes,

• So that I don't have to manually write if (!user.hasPermission(...)) in every single API handler.

Technical Requirements

1. Configuration Structure: Create a config object/map that defines rules.
• Key: Route path (support wildcards/parameters if possible, e.g., /api/users/:id).

• Key: HTTP Method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE).

• Value: Required Permission/Role (e.g., ['admin', 'editor']).

2. Middleware Logic:
• Intercept the request pipeline after UseAuthentication but before UseEndpoints.

• Resolve the current user's claims (context.User).

• Match the request path against the configuration rules.

• Validation:
• If no rule matches: Default Deny (or Default Allow, based on decision).

• If rule matches but user lacks claim: Return 403 Forbidden.

• If rule matches and user has claim: Call next().

summary: [BE] Implement Immediate Refresh Token Revocation on Permission Change
description:
Currently, if an Admin changes a user's permissions, the user retains their old access level until their JWT expires naturally. When basic refresh tokens exist, we need to secure them. If an Admin changes a user's permissions, we must invalidate all existing refresh tokens for that user immediately to prevent unauthorised access.

User Story:

• As an Admin,

• When I update a user's role or permissions,

• I want their existing refresh tokens to be immediately invalidated,

• So that they cannot perform actions they are no longer authorised to do.

Technical tasks:

1. Add columns into the user table: TokenVersion (integer) and PermissionsUpdatedAt(timestamp)

2. When the admin changes the permission for one user:
1. Increment User.TokenVersion by 1

2. Update User.PermissionsUpdatedAt to the current timestamp

3. When generating a Refresh Token, include the current TokenVersion inside the token payload (or store it in the RefreshTokens table).

4. Refresh Logic (POST /auth/refresh-token):
• Fetch the User from DB.

• Compare User.TokenVersion vs RefreshToken.Version.

• If User.TokenVersion > RefreshToken.Version:
• Return 403 Forbidden (The token is from an old "era").

• Mark the refresh token as revoked in the DB.

Acceptance Criteria

• [ ] Database column TokenVersion exists.

• [ ] Manually changing TokenVersion in the DB causes the /refresh-token endpoint to reject existing tokens for that user.

• [ ] Updating User Permissions automatically increments TokenVersion.
